newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ANC leadership to seek amnesty - report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ANC leadership to seek amnesty - report.

text.p: The entire national leadership of the African National Congress (ANC) from 1961 to 1994 is expected to apply to South Africa's truth commission for amnesty, a leading newspaper said on Friday.
The possible exception was President Nelson Mandela who has remained above party involvement with the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, Business Day said, quoting drafters of the ANC submission.
The ruling party's military and political leaders would publicly accept overall responsibility for the actions of its field operatives in the armed struggle against apartheid, the paper said.
Senior ANC leaders likely to ask for amnesty include Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, expected to succeed Mandela after the next general election in 1999, and a number of cabinet ministers.

The truth commission's mandate is to heal the wounds of apartheid by exposing as much as possible of the crimes and human rights abuses committed by both sides of the apartheid divide. It has powers to give amnesty for those who confess.
